name: cavemio-doc-comments
title: Doc comments
description: Review threads beside the text they quote: the one you choose lines up with its line, and the rest make way.

cavemio.accessibility:
- Each thread is an article named by its author and the words it quotes ("Priya Nair on “Tuesday, October 24”, 1 reply"), in the order the quotes appear, so Tab walks the document's threads from top to bottom. Enter opens one, Escape lets it go, ⌘ or Ctrl+Enter sends what you typed.
- The Comment pill can be reached with Ctrl+Alt+M while text is selected. New threads, replies, failures and resolves are announced in a status region.
- An anchor is the quote plus up to 32 characters either side, so the same words twice in a document find the right one, and edits elsewhere don't move it. Highlights are boxes drawn in a layer under the text from the quote's line rectangles, measured again only when the document changes size or content.
- Cards move by transform only; heights are measured from what's inside each card, so a card easing open never makes the margin re-solve on every frame.
- Reduced motion places cards, opens threads and resolves in place; highlights, rings and the Undo line still say what happened.
cavemio.previewNote: Interactive local fixture. Data and async results are simulated in the preview; the caller supplies application services.

props.name: children
props.description: – · The document. Any markup; it's read to find quotes and never changed.

props.name: threads / defaultThreads
props.description: – · { id, anchor: { quote, prefix?, suffix? }, comments: { id, author, body, createdAt }[], resolved? }. Resolved threads aren't shown; a thread whose quote can't be found waits until it can.

props.name: onThreadsChange
props.description: – · Every new thread, reply and resolve.

props.name: onCreate
props.description: – · Turns on commenting on a selection. Resolve with the stored thread; throw to keep the words and offer Try again.

props.name: onReply
props.description: – · Turns on replies. Resolve with the stored comment; throw to keep the words and offer Try again.

props.name: onResolve
props.description: – · Turns on ✓. Runs once the chance to undo is over; throw to open the thread again.

props.name: undoFor
props.description: 4000 · How long Undo is offered after resolving, ms.

useCases.title: Specs and documents under review
useCases.description: Reviewers comment on exact sentences in a spec or a proposal.

useCases.title: Contracts and approvals
useCases.description: Collect feedback on a quoted clause and mark it resolved.

useCases.title: CMS and editorial tools
useCases.description: Editors leave notes on drafts beside the text they refer to.

useCases.title: Client proposals
useCases.description: Let a client comment on a shared page without a separate tool.

features.title: Threads beside their line
features.description: Each thread sits level with the line it quotes, and threads that would overlap stack downwards.

features.title: Select text to comment
features.description: A Comment pill appears beside the selection and grows into the composer. Ctrl+Alt+M does the same from the keyboard.

features.title: Anchors survive edits
features.description: A thread finds its text by quoting it, so edits elsewhere don’t move it. Highlights sit under the text and never change it.

features.title: Replies and resolve
features.description: Replies rise in and the count rolls. Resolve holds “Resolved · Undo” for four seconds before the thread goes.

features.title: Failures keep your words
features.description: If a comment or reply fails to save, the words stay and the button reads Try again.

features.title: Works on narrow screens
features.description: Below 620px a count sits at the end of the line, and the paragraph opens a gap for the thread.

states.title: margin
states.description: Each card sits 10px above the top of its quote's first line. Cards that would overlap are pushed down, 8px apart; the margin grows to fit the last one.

states.title: focus
states.description: Choosing a thread (its card, Enter on it, or a click on its highlight) places it exactly at its line; the cards after it are pushed below it and the cards before it are pulled above it, all gliding 360ms. Its highlight deepens with an underline, its card takes a ring and opens to every reply and a reply field, its height easing 260ms.

states.title: comment
states.description: A selection in the document shows a Comment pill in the margin beside its first line (or under the selection when narrow), rising out of a blur in 220ms. The pill grows into the composer by one clip in 320ms; the selection becomes a highlight so it stays visible while you type. Ctrl+Alt+M does the same from the keyboard.

states.title: post
states.description: Comment shows Posting while onCreate runs, then the composer becomes the thread in the same card. A reply rises 4px out of a blur and the "2 replies" count rolls. If either throws, the words stay and the button says Try again.

states.title: resolve
states.description: ✓ fades the highlight (320ms) and turns the card into "Resolved · Undo" over a thin line that drains for 4s (paused while hovered). Then onResolve runs and the card goes while the others glide up; if it throws, the thread opens again with a note.

states.title: narrow
states.description: Below 620px there's no margin: a speech-bubble count sits beside the first line of each thread. Choosing it opens a gap under the paragraph (its margin eases 280ms) and the card sits in the gap, so nothing covers the text.
